title: Gospel Parallels
description: The life, death, and resurrection of Jesus across all four Gospels, harmonized into one reading sequence — each evangelist contributing the movement he tells best.
audience: Anyone who wants to read the whole story of Jesus once, in order, using all four witnesses.

sequence.note: Begin before Bethlehem: who this child actually is.
The fullest birth narrative — annunciation, Magnificat, manger, Simeon.
Matthew adds the magi, Herod, and the flight to Egypt.
Baptism and the wilderness temptation.
The early ministry the synoptics skip: Cana, Nicodemus, the Samaritan woman.
Galilee at Mark's breakneck pace.
The Sermon on the Mount.
The miracles and the sending of the Twelve.
Parables by the sea; the storm, the demoniac, Jairus' daughter.
Luke's road teaching: Good Samaritan, Lord's Prayer, banquets.
Loaves, blindness, and Peter's half-sighted confession.
The great claims: bread of life, light of the world, I AM.
The confession and the Transfiguration.
Down the mountain toward Jerusalem: the way of the cross.
The lost-and-found parables and Zacchaeus, on the final approach.
The man born blind, the good shepherd, Lazarus — the sign that seals the plot.
Palm Sunday and the temple cleared.
The fig tree, the widow's coins, the temple's doom.
Final controversies and the Olivet Discourse.
The upper room: foot-washing, farewell, the great prayer.
The Last Supper, Gethsemane, the cross — and Emmaus.
Mark's stark passion: the cry, the torn curtain, the centurion.
Matthew's passion and the earthquake at the empty tomb.
'It is finished' — then Mary, Thomas, and breakfast on the shore.
